children: The U.S. Treasury Department is formulating rules for biopharma companies investing in China that would likely maintain their ability to ink most licensing deals for drugs originating in the country, Reuters reported on Friday, citing three sources familiar with the matter.

If finalized, the rules are expected to allow U.S. companies to invest in cutting-edge new medicines being advanced by Chinese firms as long as they are not related to pathogens or biotechnology that could be weaponized, the sources said.

The rules haven't been finalized yet and are subject to amendments, especially if President Donald Trump intervenes, said the people who have been made aware of ​the process. They sought anonymity because they are not authorized to speak publicly about the developments.

The move comes as Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to meet with his American counterpart next week, at a time when other U.S. industries are seeing a tighter regulatory environment in relation to their business dealings in China as a result of new national security legislation.
The Treasury and White House officials declined to comment, according to Reuters.

title: Trump administration is said to weigh allowing most pharma licensing deals with China
